wave: D — finishing the rounds the spend limit cut short (camera feedback bug closed)
note: Wave D. The camera feedback bug is fixed and verified: api.pitch was publishing the obstruction lift as framing pitch, combat.js servoed on it and subtracted the lift from the player's own elevation, and the loop closed on itself — the same pose measured 57.1 and 19.9 degrees on two runs. A private boomPitch now carries the lift. Re-probed on canonical, every pose is run-to-run stable and the horizon is in frame everywhere. Performance is still unmeasured: the stale lane servers were cleared but the run was cut short, and the box is now busy with unrelated work, so no fps number was recorded rather than a dirty one.

pieces.name: grass · pampas fields
pieces.gap: SHADOWS LANDED AND MERGED (+123/-16 in grass.js). Both the instanced blades and the ground carpet now sample the suns shadow map, using the pattern trees.js already had. Measured against the same grass lit, in-frame to cancel albedo: shadowed value 42.7% (target 40-45%), red x0.33, blue x1.34 — a genuine hue rotation to cool, not just a brightness cut. Lit grass unchanged at 99.6% luminance. Cost measured by A/B/A under identical contention: 0-6%, mean ~3%. Pose 01 still shows no canopy shadow and that is NOT a grass bug — proven by rendering bare terrain, which has always sampled shadows, and finding none there either: the sun sits 19.1 deg altitude dead ahead so every shadow points at the viewer and hides behind its caster. Awaiting fresh critic.

pieces.name: sky · sun · light rig
pieces.gap: FIRST REAL JUDGMENT: 2/3/2, hobby not uncertain. NAMED GAP: nothing in any frame casts a shadow — grass under a wide tree canopy measures identical in brightness to open field — so the low warm key is a directionless ambient wash. CAUSE PROVEN: grass.js never samples the shadow map (trees.js has a working sunShadow() doing exactly that, terrain receives, grass does not), and grass covers the ground in every frame. Also named, for later rounds: no sun disc at all (brightest pixel 246, none above 250); the vignette is impersonating aerial perspective and inverts the depth ramp so near grass is darker than the far ridge; 22-28% of pixels clip a channel against 0.25% in the reference; night is a blue multiply over grey (median value 0.506 vs 0.161 reference) with no moonlight direction.

pieces.name: water · ocean, rivers, foam
pieces.gap: IN BUILD on the named gap: give the sea a deep-water absorption colour so it stops rendering as the sky and sits darker and cooler than it, resolving the horizon into a line. Targets to beat: ocean currently measures brighter than the sky above it (red 251 vs 236), 23-30% of ocean pixels clipped at 254, largest row-to-row step through the horizon only ~6/255, night sea luminance sd 3.7/255.

pieces.name: horse · gaits and riding
pieces.gap: FIRST JUDGMENT: 2/2/2 (form, surface, believability), hobby not uncertain, three automatic fails (seams and end-cap discs at every leg joint, floating geometry — withers rods, a girth hoop clear of the belly, reins ending in mid-air — and a wholly untextured hide measuring 0.8-6.6/255 of detail). NAMED GAP: the torso is one smooth capsule tapering to a rounded bullet at the rear, topline dead flat within 3px across the whole loin-and-croup span, so the horse has no hindquarters at all; it needs a croup rising above the loin, a gluteal mass whose point of buttock projects back past the tail root, and a stifle bulging forward.

pieces.name: camera · cinematography
pieces.gap: FIX VERIFIED ON CANONICAL AND MERGED. api.pitch published the obstruction lift as the framing pitch, and its one external consumer — the servo in combat.js (dPitch = 0.16 - gcam.pitch, written into inp.look.y) — read the lift back out and subtracted it from pitchUser, the elevation camera.js promises is never stolen back. Closed positive feedback. A separate private boomPitch now carries the lift; only the framing pitch leaves the file. PROOF, tools/probe-campitch.mjs, two runs of every pose on the canonical checkout: 06-forest, the lock-on pose that gave 57.1 and 19.9 degrees before, now reads 8.8 and 9.2. Every pose is run-to-run stable (14.3/14.3, 13.9/13.9, 9.2/9.2, 8.6/9.2) and the horizon is in frame everywhere at NDC 0.32-0.75, against the off-screen floor-plan framing before. The boom itself still varies between runs in the combat poses (04-river-valley 17.6 vs 11.1) — the obstruction ladder finding different solutions on uneven ground, which is its job now that it no longer leaks into framing.

pieces.name: audio · score and ambience
pieces.gap: Instrument BUILT — tools/audio-render.sh, the script audio.js renderOffline() promised in a comment but which nobody ever wrote. That missing script is why audio was never judged. Levels are healthy: peak -3.1 to -3.4 dBFS, rms -13 to -17, 98% non-silent, no clipping, no DC offset. FOUND: a content-independent broadband amplitude dip every 380-450ms (autocorrelation r=0.35-0.47) in all three ambient scenarios, visible as evenly spaced full-spectrum gaps. Proven NOT to be the renderer — identical at 4x finer stepping. Cause is in the audio graph and is not yet isolated.
